isolate.title: Pick the panel that answers the question
isolate.narration: The two panels disagree. Click the series in the panel whose calculation answers the incident question, so every panel filters to it.

demonstration.narration: I'll click the series in the panel whose calculation answers the incident question, then check how both panels count.
demonstration.reasoning: Two panels can disagree because they count different things. Selecting the one that matches the question, then inspecting both, separates a real contradiction from different definitions.
demonstration.evidence: Every panel now filters to ${var.value}. That series counts transactions only; the other panel counts every event, spans included.

inspect.narration: Inspect how each panel calculates its number and confirm which one answers the incident question.

demonstration.narration: I'll open Inspect on ${var.panel} and read its request, to see exactly which events it counts.
demonstration.reasoning: A chart is an aggregate and can be misread if its formula, buckets or filters are misunderstood. The inspector shows the request behind the number.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted line is why: this panel's request keeps only processor.event: transaction, while Payment errors (all events) has no such filter. ${truth.conclusion}
